newsitem.title: USA: Enron questions Ore. cost savings estimate.
newsitem.headline: Enron questions Ore. cost savings estimate.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co on Friday questioned some of the assumptions made by staff of the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) in a review of the companies' merger plans.
"We have a long way to go in understanding if a rate cut can be supported by any cost savings from the merger," said Al Alexanderson, senior vice president of Portland General.

In a preliminary review released Thursday, the Oregon commission staff advised that approval of the merger be contingent on an annual rate cut for Portland General's customers of $47.4 million for four years.
The rate cut would then fall to $11.2 million per year until the utility's next rate case.

Mike Myers, program manager for the OPUC, said the recommendation was based on cost savings generated by the merger, compensation for PGE's trading floor which will be absorbed by Enron's and revenue that PGE's trading operations would have generated.
Assets such as the good-will of the utility name were also factored into the rate cut proposal, he said.
But Alexanderson said the OPUC staff's estimate of annual savings of $10 million after the merger was well above the companies' estimate of $3 million in annual savings.
"We are not far enough down the path of integration to really be sure of what the cost savings will be," he noted.
He also questioned their calculation of how much profit would be generated by PGE's trading operations and what the cost of maintaining trading operations would be.

Geoff Roberts, managing director of Enron Capital & Trade Resources, said the number of issues outstanding with the OPUC staff has been cut significantly since the merger plans were announced in August.
He said further progress was expected next Wednesday through Friday when a conference held by the OPUC on the merger takes place in Salem.
Roberts declined to comment on whether the rate cut stipulation would alter the merger plans, noting he "wouldn't want to speculate on negotiations."
The OPUC staff is due to make a final merger recommendation by January 31, with the commission scheduled to make its decision March 17.
